description: Composed relational pipelines: every test runs ONE query that stacks several features - joins (inner / left / full / asof), chained and recursive CTEs, LATERAL (correlated inline view and FLATTEN, including outer => TRUE), window functions (the rank family, frames, LAG/LEAD defaults, window-over-window) and QUALIFY (inline window, select-list alias, over GROUP BY). The point is the INTERACTION of the stages, which no single-feature test exercises: QUALIFY evaluating windows over grouped joins, FLATTEN output feeding further joins, a recursive CTE's result carrying a window, deduplication via ROW_NUMBER over UNION ALL. Fixtures are small and integer-valued so every expectation is hand-computable, Eve deliberately has no orders, and every query carries a full ORDER BY so embedded and live row order agree. Converted 1:1 from query/ComposedRelationalQueryTest (now retired); the Java asserted cell by cell through a helper, which the converted tests state as whole ordered row sets.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, region VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1, 'Alice', 'EMEA'), (2, 'Bob', 'EMEA'), (3, 'Cara', 'APAC'), (4, 'Dan', 'APAC'), (5, 'Eve', 'AMER')
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER, customer_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER, d DATE)

WITH totals AS (SELECT c.region, c.name, SUM(o.amount) AS total FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.region, c.name), ranked AS (SELECT region, name, total, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY total DESC) AS r FROM totals) SELECT region, name, total FROM ranked WHERE r = 1 ORDER BY region
CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, region VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1, 'Alice', 'EMEA'), (2, 'Bob', 'EMEA'), (3, 'Cara', 'APAC'), (4, 'Dan', 'APAC'), (5, 'Eve', 'AMER')
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER, customer_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER, d DATE)

SELECT c.region, c.name, SUM(o.amount) AS total FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.region, c.name QUALIFY RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY c.region ORDER BY SUM(o.amount) DESC) = 1 ORDER BY c.region
CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, region VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1, 'Alice', 'EMEA'), (2, 'Bob', 'EMEA'), (3, 'Cara', 'APAC'), (4, 'Dan', 'APAC'), (5, 'Eve', 'AMER')
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER, customer_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER, d DATE)

SELECT c.name, COALESCE(SUM(o.amount), 0) AS total, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(SUM(o.amount), 0) DESC, c.name) AS rn FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.name QUALIFY rn <= 3 ORDER BY rn
CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, region VARCHAR)

CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER, customer_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER, d DATE)
CREATE TABLE order_tags (order_id INTEGER, tags VARIANT)
INSERT INTO order_tags SELECT 101, PARSE_JSON('["rush","gift"]')
INSERT INTO order_tags SELECT 103, PARSE_JSON('["rush"]')
INSERT INTO order_tags SELECT 105, PARSE_JSON('["bulk","rush"]')
INSERT INTO order_tags SELECT 107, PARSE_JSON('["gift"]')

WITH tagged AS (SELECT t.order_id, f.value::VARCHAR AS tag FROM order_tags t, LATERAL FLATTEN(input => t.tags) f) SELECT c.region, tg.tag, COUNT(*) AS uses FROM tagged tg JOIN orders o ON o.id = tg.order_id JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.region, tg.tag QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.region ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, tg.tag) = 1 ORDER BY c.region

CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER, customer_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER, d DATE)
SELECT c.name, m.top_amount FROM customers c, LATERAL (SELECT MAX(o.amount) AS top_amount FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id) m WHERE c.region = 'EMEA' ORDER BY c.name

SELECT o.id, f.value::VARCHAR AS tag FROM orders o LEFT JOIN order_tags t ON t.order_id = o.id, LATERAL FLATTEN(input => t.tags, outer => TRUE) f QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY o.id ORDER BY COALESCE(f.value::VARCHAR, '')) = 1 ORDER BY o.id
CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, region VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1, 'Alice', 'EMEA'), (2, 'Bob', 'EMEA'), (3, 'Cara', 'APAC'), (4, 'Dan', 'APAC'), (5, 'Eve', 'AMER')
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER, customer_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER, d DATE)

WITH daily AS (SELECT o.d, SUM(o.amount) AS day_total FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE c.region IN ('EMEA', 'APAC') GROUP BY o.d) SELECT TO_CHAR(d, 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS day, day_total, SUM(day_total) OVER (ORDER BY d ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running, SUM(day_total) OVER (ORDER BY d ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS moving2 FROM daily ORDER BY d
CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, region VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1, 'Alice', 'EMEA'), (2, 'Bob', 'EMEA'), (3, 'Cara', 'APAC'), (4, 'Dan', 'APAC'), (5, 'Eve', 'AMER')
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER, customer_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER, d DATE)

WITH seq AS (SELECT c.name, o.d, o.amount FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id) SELECT name, amount, LAG(amount, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY name ORDER BY d) AS prev, LEAD(amount, 1, -1) OVER (PARTITION BY name ORDER BY d) AS next FROM seq WHERE name IN ('Alice', 'Bob') ORDER BY name, d
CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, region VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1, 'Alice', 'EMEA'), (2, 'Bob', 'EMEA'), (3, 'Cara', 'APAC'), (4, 'Dan', 'APAC'), (5, 'Eve', 'AMER')
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER, customer_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER, d DATE)

WITH jan AS (SELECT c.name, SUM(o.amount) AS a FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.d < '2026-02-01'::DATE GROUP BY c.name), feb AS (SELECT c.name, SUM(o.amount) AS a FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.d >= '2026-02-01'::DATE GROUP BY c.name) SELECT COALESCE(j.name, f.name) AS name, COALESCE(j.a, 0) AS jan_amt, COALESCE(f.a, 0) AS feb_amt, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(j.a, 0) + COALESCE(f.a, 0) DESC, COALESCE(j.name, f.name)) AS r FROM jan j FULL OUTER JOIN feb f ON f.name = j.name ORDER BY r
CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, region VARCHAR)

CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER, customer_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER, d DATE)
CREATE TABLE org (emp VARCHAR, mgr VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO org VALUES ('root', NULL), ('b1', 'root'), ('b2', 'root'), ('c1', 'b1'), ('c2', 'b1'), ('d1', 'c1')

WITH RECURSIVE chain (emp, depth) AS (SELECT emp, 1 FROM org WHERE mgr IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT o.emp, chain.depth + 1 FROM org o JOIN chain ON o.mgr = chain.emp) SELECT emp, depth, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY depth) AS peers FROM chain QUALIFY peers = 2 ORDER BY depth, emp

CREATE TABLE ticks (sym VARCHAR, t INTEGER, px INTEGER)
CREATE TABLE quotes (sym VARCHAR, t INTEGER, bid INTEGER)
INSERT INTO ticks VALUES ('A', 10, 100), ('A', 20, 110), ('B', 15, 200)
INSERT INTO quotes VALUES ('A', 5, 99), ('A', 18, 108), ('B', 30, 190)

SELECT tk.sym, tk.t, tk.px, q.bid FROM ticks tk ASOF JOIN quotes q MATCH_CONDITION (tk.t >= q.t) ON tk.sym = q.sym QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY tk.sym ORDER BY tk.t DESC) = 1 ORDER BY tk.sym
CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, region VARCHAR)

CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER, customer_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER, d DATE)

WITH busy AS (SELECT customer_id FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2) SELECT c.name, o.amount, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.id ORDER BY o.amount DESC, o.id) AS rn FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM busy b WHERE b.customer_id = c.id) QUALIFY rn = 1 ORDER BY c.name
CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, region VARCHAR)

CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER, customer_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER, d DATE)

WITH merged AS (SELECT id, amount, 1 AS src FROM orders WHERE amount >= 400 UNION ALL SELECT id, amount, 2 AS src FROM orders WHERE customer_id IN (1, 2)) SELECT id, amount, src FROM merged QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY id ORDER BY src) = 1 ORDER BY id
CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, region VARCHAR)

CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER, customer_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER, d DATE)

WITH totals AS (SELECT c.region, c.name, SUM(o.amount) AS total FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.region, c.name), shared AS (SELECT region, name, total, SUM(total) OVER (PARTITION BY region) AS region_total FROM totals) SELECT region, name, total, region_total, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY total DESC) AS r FROM shared QUALIFY r <= 2 ORDER BY region, r, name
